# Tredio

> Tredio turns what the internet is talking about into markets on NEAR.
> An AI radar finds trends, a model on NEAR AI Cloud reviews each one and signs its verdict, and an oracle scores each listed trend's attention from 0 to 100 and records it on NEAR, where the registry contract accepts only reports signed by the oracle key.
> People and agents trade that index: Up/Down outcome series settled in USDC, attention perps up to 3x, trend coins on bonding curves that graduate into Rhea Finance pools, and Hyperliquid perps on the asset behind a trend.
> Tredio is live on NEAR testnet; every balance there is a test asset with no monetary value.

## Links

- [Website](https://tredio.bid): what Tredio is and how it works.
- [App](https://app.tredio.bid): sign in with a passkey (Face ID, a fingerprint or a security key) and trade on NEAR testnet, gas-free.
- [API](https://api.tredio.bid): JSON over HTTPS; the root lists the main routes.
- [This file](https://tredio.bid/llms.txt): the reference for agents.

## API

Base URL: `https://api.tredio.bid`.
The API answers index values in points (51.86 is 51.86 points); on chain they have 6 decimals (1000000 is one point), as do USDC amounts.

- `GET /v1/status`: health of the oracle, markets and services.
- `GET /v1/trends`: live trends with their current attention index.
- `GET /v1/trends/{identifier}`: one trend and its current state.
- `GET /v1/trends/{identifier}/stats`: trading activity for one trend.
- `GET /v1/candidates`: approved candidates waiting to list, with recent readings.
- `GET /v1/reviews/{hash}`: a stored AI review and its attestation.
- `GET /v1/leaderboard/traders`: traders ranked by results.

## For agents

- MCP: `packages/mcp` in the repository is an MCP server (stdio) with tools for trends, markets, accounts, AI reviews and `verify_index`, which checks the registry's checkpoint and the oracle's signature itself.
  Its trade tools (Up/Down, perps, coins, calls) are dry runs by default and send only within the user's policy: an allowlist of tools, a USDC cap per call and a daily cap.
- Skill: `skills/tredio/SKILL.md` in the repository teaches an agent to read, verify and trade Tredio safely.
- x402: `GET /v1/x402` lists the paid routes (`GET /v1/x402/trends/{identifier}/history` for 0.01 USDC: every checkpoint and source reading; `POST /v1/x402/backtests` for 0.02 USDC).
  They follow x402 v2's NEAR `exact` scheme: the route answers 402 with `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`, the agent signs one USDC `ft_transfer` as a NEP-366 delegate action and sends it in `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`, and Tredio's relayer submits it, so the agent needs no NEAR for gas.
- Autopilot: an owner can let rules trade Hyperliquid through a revocable session on their own account; the account contract enforces the price band (2% of a fresh mark) and leverage cap (10x), and the executor enforces stop-loss and loss limits off chain.
- Verification: every index value on NEAR carries the oracle's ed25519 signature, so an agent can check a number on chain instead of trusting the API.
  The oracle's build runs in an OutLayer TEE; on testnet the registry still trusts its bootstrap key until the API the enclave reads is public.

## How it works

1. Radar: Elfa, Bluesky, Nansen, CoinGecko, GeckoTerminal, Wikipedia and other public sources propose trends.
2. Review: a verifiable model on NEAR AI Cloud checks each candidate; the signed attestation is stored with the listing.
3. Oracle: the oracle computes the attention index with a published method (its build runs in an OutLayer TEE with a key bound to the build) and writes it to Tredio's registry contract on NEAR, which accepts signed reports only.
4. Markets: each trend gets 24-hour and 7-day Up/Down series on Tredio's own order book, an attention perp and a trend coin; Hyperliquid perps on the underlying asset are placed from the user's NEAR account through Chain Signatures.
5. Accounts: passkey accounts on NEAR, with no seed phrase; one prompt opens a week-long session whose network fees a relayer pays.
6. Deposits: on mainnet, NEAR Intents 1Click brings USDC in from other chains; testnet shows dry quotes.
